drills.q: Recite the 9-phase design sequence with its 45-minute timebox.
drills.a: Restate(2) / requirements(5) / numbers(5) / API(5) / data model(7) / architecture(8) / scale(6) / failure(5) / wrap(2).

drills.q: Why compute a capacity number before you know what decision it will drive?
drills.a: You shouldn't -- state the use before computing it ('I need QPS to decide if one Postgres primary suffices'). Numbers that never feed a downstream decision are theater, not rigor.

drills.q: URL shortener: what's the actual hard problem, and why does hashing-and-retry degrade?
drills.a: Short-code generation without collision at scale. Random-and-retry degrades as the keyspace fills (collision rate rises); prefer base62 encoding of an auto-incrementing ID or a pre-generated code pool.

drills.q: Distributed rate limiter: two requests hit two different API servers in the same millisecond, both check Redis under the limit, both proceed. What's the fix?
drills.a: An atomic check-and-increment (a Lua script in Redis, or INCR with expiry evaluated atomically) instead of a separate GET-then-SET, which is the actual race.

drills.q: Real-time leaderboard, 10M DAU, needs top-100 and any user's rank on demand. What data structure, and why does a SQL window-function-per-request approach fail?
drills.a: A sorted set (Redis ZSET) -- O(log n) insert/update, O(log n + k) range query, O(log n) rank lookup. A live ranked SQL query or full re-sort per write can't keep up with this write volume.

drills.q: 200 leaderboards, some with 10 users, some with 2M, sharing infrastructure. Does one Redis ZSET per leaderboard still work?
drills.a: Not uniformly -- this becomes a sharding/resource-allocation problem, not a single-leaderboard scaling problem. Colocate small leaderboards, isolate or further partition large ones.

drills.q: Support ticket volume triples overnight; your GenAI cost triples with it. What are your real levers?
drills.a: Semantic caching (keyed on query embedding, not exact match) for repeated/similar queries, a cheaper model for first-pass triage with escalation only when needed, or a hard per-tenant/per-hour cost ceiling with graceful degradation -- not 'just pay for it.'

drills.q: Two customers add the last unit of an item to their cart within 50ms of each other. Trace exactly what happens and what the losing customer sees.
drills.a: One request acquires a reservation/lock on the last unit first; the second request's response must be an honest 'out of stock,' not a silent oversell from a race. 'The database handles it' is not an answer -- name the mechanism (transaction with row-level lock, or a reservation token with TTL).

drills.q: Finance wants dollar cost per million tokens split by interactive vs batch workload, and you don't have it. What should have existed already?
drills.a: Per-workload cost attribution requires the batch and interactive paths to be separately instrumented and ideally separately billed infrastructure from day one -- retrofitting cost attribution onto a shared, unlabeled GPU pool afterward is expensive and imprecise.

drills.q: What single line does an interviewer use at minute 20 if there's no data model yet, and what should you do in response?
drills.a: 'We're almost halfway through and I don't have a data model. Let's move.' Response: stop elaborating requirements/API, commit to tables and a partition key immediately, derived from the access pattern already stated.

drills.q: What defines the NO HIRE band (5-8/20) in the design round rubric?
drills.a: Boxes drawn early with no derivation; no numbers, or numbers never referenced again; cannot answer 'why this and not X' for any major decision; struggles to recover from an interrupt even after a second prompt.
